purpose: Compose generic tenant, resource, capability, lifecycle, access, audit, import, and reconciliation presentation from canonical Ten4Seven components without moving platform authority into the UI system.

tenant-selector.purpose: Present a consumer-supplied organization context choice without deciding membership, entitlement, or navigation authority.
consumerInputs: opaque organization identifiers and labels
current organization identifier
available organization options
selection callback and persistence policy
systemOwns: canonical component composition
labels, keyboard behavior, focus, and responsive presentation
semantic state and status styling through shared tokens
invocation of consumer-provided action elements
consumerOwns: membership and entitlement meaning
which organizations are available to the principal
selection persistence and any data refresh
route changes or API commands after selection

responsive.desktop: Place the selector in the shell context slot or route header.
responsive.tablet: Keep the selected organization visible while wrapping the option control.
responsive.mobile: Use a full-width labelled select or consumer-owned drawer entry.

accessibility: Use one visible label and expose the selected organization as text.
Keep the native select or canonical popup keyboard reachable.
Announce loading, empty, and error context without relying on color.
tenant-selector.aiGuidance: Choose this pattern when a user needs to change the current organization context; use a consumer-owned callback for the resulting route or data change.
antiPatterns: Filtering organizations with a local permission rule
Fetching or mutating membership inside the selector
Using a visual brand mark as the only organization name

resource-selector.purpose: Present a flat or hierarchical resource choice such as a site, facility, workspace, or location while leaving scope meaning to the consumer.
consumerInputs: opaque resource identifiers, labels, descriptions, and hierarchy
selected resource identifiers
disabled-node presentation supplied by the consumer
selection callback and scope persistence policy
systemOwns: canonical component composition
labels, keyboard behavior, focus, and responsive presentation
semantic state and status styling through shared tokens
invocation of consumer-provided action elements
consumerOwns: resource availability and scope meaning
which nodes are disabled and why
authorization, server-side validation, and persistence
what changes after a resource selection

responsive.desktop: Keep a bounded hierarchy beside the selected context.
responsive.tablet: Retain ancestry and selection while reducing supporting copy.
responsive.mobile: Use a bounded tree or consumer-owned drawer; never expand page height without limit.

accessibility: Use tree semantics for nested resources and expose ancestry through labels.
Preserve Arrow, Home, End, Space, and Enter interaction from HierarchyPicker.
Keep partial, disabled, empty, and selected states available as text or semantics.
resource-selector.aiGuidance: Choose this pattern when the resource has ancestry or a scope boundary; use a flat Select or Combobox only when the choice is genuinely flat.
antiPatterns: Naming the generic primitive after one business product
Hiding disabled resources without a consumer explanation
Conflating resource selection with authorization evaluation

module-catalog.purpose: Present a consumer-supplied catalog of capabilities, availability, current state, and next action in a consistent bounded collection.
consumerInputs: module identifiers, labels, descriptions, and category
consumer-supplied module state and availability copy
action elements for setup, inspection, or support
current organization/resource context
systemOwns: canonical component composition
labels, keyboard behavior, focus, and responsive presentation
semantic state and status styling through shared tokens
invocation of consumer-provided action elements
consumerOwns: module registry data and ordering
availability, entitlement, and lifecycle state
action behavior, navigation, and persistence
whether a capability is relevant in the current context

responsive.desktop: Use a compact card or table collection with state and next action aligned.
responsive.tablet: Wrap cards and keep state/action visible before supporting descriptions.
responsive.mobile: Stack modules with the state label and primary action in each card.

accessibility: Give the collection a named region and each module a visible heading.
Write availability and next action in text; color and icon are supplementary.
Keep setup, inspect, and support actions keyboard reachable in reading order.
module-catalog.aiGuidance: Choose this pattern when users need to browse capabilities and understand which next action applies to each one.
antiPatterns: Treating a catalog card as proof of entitlement
Showing every module as active because the fixture has no backend
Creating a product-specific module card primitive

module-activation.purpose: Present consumer-supplied lifecycle checkpoints and progress without triggering, retrying, or calculating provisioning work.
consumerInputs: ordered lifecycle checkpoints and consumer-calculated percentages
current module state and freshness context
consumer-owned retry, support, or inspect actions
activity or evidence supplied by the platform
systemOwns: canonical component composition
labels, keyboard behavior, focus, and responsive presentation
semantic state and status styling through shared tokens
invocation of consumer-provided action elements
consumerOwns: lifecycle state transitions and provisioning authority
progress calculation, freshness, and retry policy
side effects, API commands, and polling
whether a failed dependency is recoverable

responsive.desktop: Keep checkpoints and current lifecycle context visible together.
responsive.tablet: Stack supporting activity below the selected checkpoint detail.
responsive.mobile: Use the bounded milestone sequence followed by current state and action.

accessibility: Expose each checkpoint as ordered keyboard-reachable milestone content.
Expose determinate progress with its label and numeric value.
Do not auto-advance or silently mutate a lifecycle state from the renderer.
module-activation.aiGuidance: Choose this pattern when platform or product code supplies lifecycle checkpoints and the user needs progress plus a safe next action.
antiPatterns: Starting provisioning from a visual component mount
Inferring percentage from milestone labels
Using a spinner without a state, checkpoint, or recovery explanation

setup-checklist.purpose: Present ordered setup requirements and completion supplied by a consumer before a module or capability can be used.
consumerInputs: ordered requirements, completion state, and labels
completion percentage and current requirement
resolution copy and action elements
read-only or unavailable reason when applicable
systemOwns: canonical component composition
labels, keyboard behavior, focus, and responsive presentation
semantic state and status styling through shared tokens
invocation of consumer-provided action elements
consumerOwns: requirement truth, ordering, and completion evaluation
validation, persistence, and setup side effects
which action resolves a requirement
whether the checklist is applicable to the current context

responsive.desktop: Keep the checklist beside the module summary or context.
responsive.tablet: Stack requirement detail below the selected checklist stage.
responsive.mobile: Use one ordered vertical sequence with each action adjacent to its requirement.

accessibility: Expose the ordered checklist and percentage as labelled progress semantics.
Keep incomplete requirements and their resolution action adjacent in DOM order.
Do not represent completion only through a check color or icon.
setup-checklist.aiGuidance: Choose this pattern when a user needs to complete a bounded set of consumer-owned prerequisites.
antiPatterns: Calculating readiness from checklist labels in Ten4Seven
Hiding incomplete requirements behind a decorative progress ring
Auto-submitting or auto-advancing setup steps

module-state-presentation.purpose: Render normalized module availability, access, lifecycle, and action-required states supplied by a consumer.
consumerInputs: normalized module state identifier
applicability and authorization context
title, description, details, and action elements
freshness or lifecycle evidence when relevant
systemOwns: canonical component composition
labels, keyboard behavior, focus, and responsive presentation
semantic state and status styling through shared tokens
invocation of consumer-provided action elements
the normalized 11-state vocabulary and default semantic metadata
aria-labelledby and aria-describedby wiring for the state surface
consumerOwns: state applicability and mapping from platform lifecycle
permission, entitlement, tenant, and resource decisions
copy overrides, actions, and event handlers
lifecycle mutations and route behavior

responsive.desktop: Keep state copy and the next action in one bounded surface.
responsive.tablet: Preserve the state title and action before secondary details.
responsive.mobile: Stack state, explanation, details, and actions in document order.

accessibility: State the meaning in visible text and supplement it with semantic iconography.
Associate the state title and description with the semantic section.
Keep consumer-provided actions keyboard reachable and independently labelled.
module-state-presentation.aiGuidance: Choose this pattern when a consumer has already determined a module state and Ten4Seven should present the explanation and next action.
antiPatterns: Calling canAccess or evaluating entitlement in the renderer
Fetching tenant or resource context from ModuleState
Mutating provisioning, suspension, or permission state from a CTA

permission-scope.purpose: Present consumer-supplied permission-denied, out-of-scope, and read-only explanations beside the relevant resource context.
consumerInputs: consumer-supplied permission or scope presentation state
resource hierarchy and selected/disabled nodes
reason, owner, support, or request-access actions
read-only capability details when available
systemOwns: canonical component composition
labels, keyboard behavior, focus, and responsive presentation
semantic state and status styling through shared tokens
invocation of consumer-provided action elements
consumerOwns: effective access and resource scope evaluation
why the principal is denied or limited
request, support, escalation, and navigation behavior
server-side enforcement and audit authority

responsive.desktop: Keep scope context and the access explanation side by side.
responsive.tablet: Stack resource context before the denial explanation and action.
responsive.mobile: Use one vertical sequence with the reason before any request/support action.

accessibility: Write the denied or limited condition in text and do not rely on a lock icon alone.
Keep the resource hierarchy labelled and keyboard navigable.
Make request/support actions reachable without making the disabled business action focusable.
permission-scope.aiGuidance: Choose this pattern when the consumer needs to explain a supplied access or scope result without exposing an authorization rule in the UI system.
antiPatterns: Treating a hidden option as a permission explanation
Putting authorization policy in a button disabled condition inside the pattern
Calling a generic hierarchy Farm-only

permission-matrix.purpose: Present a readable consumer-owned comparison of roles and capability outcomes using canonical table semantics.
consumerInputs: role labels and opaque identifiers
capability labels and consumer-evaluated outcomes
table ordering, filters, and any row actions
read-only or unavailable presentation state
systemOwns: canonical component composition
labels, keyboard behavior, focus, and responsive presentation
semantic state and status styling through shared tokens
invocation of consumer-provided action elements
consumerOwns: role, capability, and effective access semantics
policy evaluation and changes to membership
which cells are authoritative and when they are fresh
editing, persistence, and audit of role changes

responsive.desktop: Use a comparable table with stable role and capability columns.
responsive.tablet: Keep the matrix in a bounded scroll owner and preserve row/column labels.
responsive.mobile: Use the canonical stacked table projection only when comparison semantics remain clear.

accessibility: Give the table a caption and explicit column headers.
Write capability outcomes as text or labelled status chips, not color alone.
Preserve the table's bounded scroll or stacked semantics on narrow screens.
permission-matrix.aiGuidance: Choose this pattern for a read-oriented role/capability comparison; move editing into a consumer-owned form or bounded workflow.
antiPatterns: Calculating effective access in a table cell renderer
Using a grid of unlabeled color dots as the permission contract
Forcing a wide matrix into unreadable cards without a declared projection

activity-audit.purpose: Present consumer-supplied chronological activity and evidence-oriented audit events without claiming storage or immutability.
consumerInputs: ordered events with actor, action, object, and timestamp
source, evidence, result, and state-change details when available
empty/loading/error presentation state
consumer-owned filtering or detail actions
systemOwns: canonical component composition
labels, keyboard behavior, focus, and responsive presentation
semantic state and status styling through shared tokens
invocation of consumer-provided action elements
consumerOwns: event truth, ordering, freshness, and source
audit storage, immutability, retention, and export
actor identity and business interpretation
filters, pagination, and detail navigation

responsive.desktop: Keep the ordered trace beside current context when useful.
responsive.tablet: Move trace below current work while preserving event order.
responsive.mobile: Use one chronological column with actor, action, and timestamp together.

accessibility: Use ordered-list semantics and keep each timestamp and actor as text.
Do not communicate event results only through an icon or status color.
Keep filters and event detail actions keyboard reachable if supplied.
activity-audit.aiGuidance: Use this pattern when users need a readable history or evidence trace; do not infer immutable audit authority from a visual feed.
antiPatterns: Treating activity and audit as identical product guarantees
Dropping actor, timestamp, object, or source context
Appending arbitrary prose instead of structured events

import-exception-review.purpose: Present consumer-owned import progress, row outcomes, and exception review actions using canonical files, progress, alert, and table contracts.
consumerInputs: consumer-owned file or import metadata
determinate or indeterminate progress value
row-level exception reason and suggested next action
retry, download, inspect, or discard action elements
systemOwns: canonical component composition
labels, keyboard behavior, focus, and responsive presentation
semantic state and status styling through shared tokens
invocation of consumer-provided action elements
consumerOwns: file parsing, validation, import authority, and persistence
progress calculation and job lifecycle
exception meaning, correction policy, and retry side effects
download/export content and access control

responsive.desktop: Keep import summary, progress, and exception rows in a bounded review grid.
responsive.tablet: Stack exception detail below progress before secondary actions.
responsive.mobile: Keep progress and the first recovery action before the scrollable exception table.

accessibility: Name the upload and progress controls and expose numeric progress when determinate.
Give the exception table a caption and plain-language reason column.
Keep row actions keyboard reachable and never imply success from color alone.
import-exception-review.aiGuidance: Choose this pattern when an import has measurable progress and exceptions that require accountable review.
antiPatterns: Uploading or parsing a file inside a presentational pattern
Hiding failed rows behind a success percentage
Making retry a side effect of rendering an exception row

mapping-reconciliation.purpose: Present consumer-supplied source/target mapping outcomes, matched and unmatched counts, and review state without calculating reconciliation.
consumerInputs: source and target labels or identifiers
consumer-calculated match, mismatch, and unresolved outcomes
progress or completion values with their basis
review, correction, or evidence action elements
systemOwns: canonical component composition
labels, keyboard behavior, focus, and responsive presentation
semantic state and status styling through shared tokens
invocation of consumer-provided action elements
consumerOwns: mapping rules, matching logic, and reconciliation calculations
source/target data truth and freshness
correction, persistence, approval, and audit behavior
whether a mismatch is actionable or informational

responsive.desktop: Show summary progress beside the comparable mapping table.
responsive.tablet: Keep the table bounded and move evidence or revision detail below it.
responsive.mobile: Place outcome summary first, then use the canonical stacked or scroll table projection.

accessibility: Name source, target, outcome, and unresolved reasons in table headers and text.
Expose progress with a label and numeric value supplied by the consumer.
Keep review and evidence actions reachable without changing the displayed outcome.
mapping-reconciliation.aiGuidance: Choose this pattern when a consumer has already calculated source/target mapping and users need to review the resulting reconciliation status.
antiPatterns: Summing or matching records inside a table component
Calling all unresolved rows errors without consumer severity
Persisting a correction from a visual status click

responsive.desktop: Use AppShell, route context, a bounded PageHeader, and grouped pattern content with decision-relevant context first.
responsive.tablet: Collapse navigation, wrap context, reduce supporting copy, and preserve state, scope, progress, exception, and next-action semantics.
responsive.mobile: Use the canonical drawer navigation and one vertical reading order; tables remain bounded scroll or an explicit stacked projection.

accessibility: Use one route-level heading and named navigation, context, pattern, table, and progress regions.
Keep consumer-supplied state, reason, actor, timestamp, scope, and next action in text.
Preserve canonical keyboard, focus, popup, drawer, table, and hierarchy behavior.
Do not auto-advance lifecycle, apply permission decisions, or silently persist a correction.

system: semantic tokens, icons, accessibility, responsive behavior, and motion
presentation of consumer-supplied values and state identifiers
consumer: principal, tenant, organization, resource, module, role, and capability data
permission, entitlement, scope, lifecycle, import, mapping, and reconciliation decisions
fetching, mutation, persistence, handlers, routing, and audit storage
platform: principal context, effective access, tenant membership, module registry, provisioning authority, and audit semantics
